reliability.rationale: Nine whole-device tests support a modest7.7% physical-unit MAE improvement over the training-only shape template, with7/9 device wins. Three same-device anchors are explicitly supplied.

mechanism.rationale: Calibration ratio plausibly encodes turn-on shape, but an exponent near2 at low drain bias is not proof of a MOS saturation square law. The negative-side exponent hits its bound and is weakly identified.

novelty.rationale: Targeted source-paper review is disclosed. These known model families and local extensions do not establish literature priority or a new fundamental law.

significance.rationale: A compact sparse-characterization recipe that may reduce curve sampling under the same array conditions, with no measured production-cost benefit.

reproducibility.rationale: Exact states, native anchors and held-group results are present; independent computational replay is a separate review.

impact.rationale: No industrial deployment, intervention, measurement-cost experiment or external replication is included.

checks: Inspected all group results and baseline comparisons
Checked explicit calibration, target meaning and interpretation limits
limitations: One measured array with supplied same-device endpoint/interior calibration; no independent lot or environment transfer; two devices prefer the template.
